status: Figures for the Gun Deployment finder (MS/Engines/GunDeployment). R figures are written in the Pakistani books (page cited); U figures are US doctrine cited where the Pakistani books are silent; E figures are proposals for the user to correct.

basisKey.R: Written in a Pakistani book (SO's Handbook 2019, IBB, C&SC handouts, OoW, MW, DW), page cited
basisKey.U: US doctrine cited (ATP 3-09.50 2016, ATP 3-09.70 2015, FM 3-09 2024, TC 3-09.81 2016, FM 3-09.70 2000, FM 6-50 1996, FM 3-09.21 2001; the JMRC article 2024), checked against the copies kept in Material/Literature/2. Online
basisKey.E: Decision or proposal: no figure in the books or the open doctrine searched (listed under 'Looked for in'); the reason is given, with any book words it rests on as context. 'decided' = taken for the tool on the user's instruction (17 Nov 2026), to be replaced when a book figure is found
basisKey.M: Method setting of the finder: how it searches, how much data it needs before it judges, how it orders the list. Not a military rule; it never makes a site pass a check it would fail. The reason is given, and a test where one can show it

crest.method: FM 6-50 ch 6: Min QE = the greatest sum of Angles 1-5 for every gun and charge. A1 angle of site to crest; A2 vertical clearance 5 m / PCR in km (mils); A3 comp site (TFT Table G) x (A1 + A2); A4 elevation at PCR (TFT Table F col 2); A5 2 forks at PCR (TFT Table F col 6). Each angle rounded up to the next mil; PCR to the nearest 100 m. The finder works out A1 and A2 from the 30 m elevation and A4 as an estimate; A3 and A5 need the firing tables.

searchM.src: How far toward the target the finder looks for the crest that sets the minimum QE (the visible crest, ATP 3-09.50 p 8-1; crests beyond it are intervening crests, checked against the trajectory, TC 3-09.81 p 15-34). At 8 km a crest must stand over 83 m above the muzzle to give even 10 mils, so a farther crest seldom sets the minimum QE

refs.quote: determining the lowest quadrant elevation that can be safely fired from a position to ensure that projectiles clear all visible crests
Intervening crests are defined as any obstruction between the firing unit and the target not visible from the firing unit.

minM.src: The crest is looked for from one 30 m elevation cell in front of the guns: nearer obstacles (trees, walls, buildings at the pits) are not in the 30 m elevation and are measured at each gun, as FM 6-50 has the A1 measured at each howitzer

refs.quote: Piece-to-crest range (PCR) is the horizontal distance between the piece and the crest, expressed to the nearest 100 meters.
If the platoon leader determines that the high sight to crest is due to a single narrow obstruction (for example, a lone tree), that howitzer may be called out of action

muzzleM.src: The crest is measured along the bottom of the bore (TC 3-09.81 p 15-31), not from the ground; no book gives the bore height. 2 m taken: about the bore of a medium gun at low elevation (towed lower, SP higher). A lower bore gives a slightly higher angle to the crest: the GPO measures it at each gun (FM 6-50 A1)

mountains.note: MW p 240: gun areas are scarce near roads; towed guns by sections near hairpin bends; light high-trajectory guns forward on reverse slopes and in valleys. MW p 244: deploy by sections in two or three places. FM 6-50 p F-1: high-angle fire may be required.

desert.note: OoW Vol I p 70: a number of alternative gun areas; DW p 59-61: guns not to be overrun early, protect gun areas, plan successive positions in depth; guns cannot engage the reverse slopes of high steep dunes. FM 6-50 p F-5: wadis attract but flash-flood.

scan.note: Search: places tried every stepM metres within the search circle; the best `keep` (by the finer reading, at least 1.5 steps or half an area apart) read in full; at most maxSites listed, altMinM apart. Method settings (M): they set how many places are read and listed, not what passes.

frontGateFrac.src: Search shortcut: a place nearer the front than half the minimum is not read in full; it would fail Behind front anyway (that row fails anything under the minimum), so the list is the same, only quicker. Checked by tools/sitefinder-test/run.mjs

minKnownGate.src: The room shortcut acts only where the ground class is known on half the samples or more: a place with too little data is read in full and shown 'not read', never left out on a guess

checks.note: Working thresholds of the checks. None is in a book: each is a decision (E) with its reason and where it was looked for, or a method setting (M) where it only decides whether there is enough data to judge.

minKnownShare.src: A site whose ground class is known on under 60 % of its samples is shown as 'not read' (tiles missing or still loading), never passed: a judgement on less than about two thirds of the ground would be a guess (safety first)

firmWarnShare.src: No figure in any book. Over a tenth of the area soft (under the fifth that fails) needs work: matting, a recce of the soft patches, guns kept off them

crestMaxUnknown.src: Crest: when over 30 % of the line to the target has no height, the crest is 'not read' rather than judged on the part that has; the gun position officer measures it at the guns (FM 6-50 A1)

order.note: How the list is ordered: the worst check first (a site that fails anything is below one that only needs work), then the weighted share of checks passed, then the finer reading. Method settings (M): no doctrine orders sites by a score, so the order only helps reading; every row carries its own rule, and Compare shows them side by side.

toneScore.src: Weighted score: a check that passes counts 1, needs work 0.55, not read 0.4, fails 0

weightsNote.src: weights (below): room and crest 3; level, firm, air, access, range, front 2; avoid 1 - the checks a gun area cannot do without weigh most

pre.src: Finer reading (orders places with the same results, and picks which are read in full): usable room x3, level 2 / 1 / 0, firm x1.5, concealment / 1.5, BUA x-2, waterlogged x-3
